question_text: A coffee-machine brand tracks how many buyers send their machine back and how many come back to buy coffee pods. Which stage of consumption is the marketer watching?
hint: Returns and repeat purchases happen once the consumer is using the product.
correct_answer_citation: Week 01 · The Three Stages of Consumption

options.option_explanation: In prepurchase the marketer studies how consumer attitudes form. Returns and repeat purchases come later.
At the purchase stage the marketer focuses on packaging, convenience and store atmosphere, not on returns.
Correct. In postpurchase the marketer monitors satisfaction, returns, and repeat purchases.
Consumption starts when the consumer identifies a need. Returns only happen after the product has been bought and used.

question_text: A shopper grabs the same brand of toothpaste every time without looking at the other options on the shelf. What does this tell a marketer?
hint: Think about what real people have in limited supply.
correct_answer_citation: Week 01 · Why Consumers Are Not Calculators

options.option_text: The shopper compared every choice and its cost
options.option_explanation: That is the old economic model. The shopper did not look at the other options at all.

options.option_text: Habits and shortcuts are driving the decision
options.option_explanation: Correct. Real people have limited time and energy, so they use mental shortcuts, and decisions depend on habits and brand loyalty.
Perfect rationality is what old economics assumed. A buyer who never looks at the alternatives is not comparing all choices.

options.option_text: The other brands must all cost much more
options.option_explanation: Nothing says the shopper checked prices. Picking the same brand without looking is a mental shortcut.

question_text: A ski shop sends one offer to customers in snowy cities and a different offer to customers in warm, coastal cities. Which kind of segmentation is it using?
hint: The offer changes with where people live and the weather there.
correct_answer_citation: Week 01 · Market Segmentation: Who Are We Talking To?

options.option_explanation: Correct. Geographics group people by location, city size, and climate.
Demographics group people by age, gender, income, and education. The shop is splitting customers by where they live.
Behavioral segments group people by how often they buy and how they use the item. Climate is a geographic trait.
Psychographics group people by lifestyle, values, and personality. Snowy versus warm cities is about location and climate.
